title: Remark
body_md: Following \citep{xu2026moga}, we show that our assumption is realistic. Their analysis was conducted on MLP and attention blocks, and they imposed activation function regularity and bounded parameter assumptions that are consistent with our generalized abstract-residual function \cref{as2} for the corresponding MLP and Attention blocks. Our set-up is therefore a faithful abstraction of the standard conditions satisfied by modern architectures; the detailed reductions are carried out in the appendix via \cref{prop:mlp} and \cref{prop:attention}.

\bf} 
{Stage 1: Recursion.}
Differentiating the recursion for \(s_k^{(j,U_j)}\) with respect to \(W_\ell\) in direction \(\Delta V_\ell\),
\begin{align*}
h_k^{(j,\ell;U_j,V_\ell)}
&= J_k h_{k-1}^{(j,\ell;U_j,V_\ell)}
+ \alpha \partial_y^2 f_{W_k}(y_{k-1})[s_{k-1}^{(j,U_j)}, s_{k-1}^{(\ell,V_\ell)}]\\
&\quad + \alpha \mathbf{1}_{j=k} \partial_y \partial_{W_k} f_{W_k}(y_{k-1})[s_{k-1}^{(\ell,V_\ell)}, \Delta U_k]\\
&\quad + \alpha \mathbf{1}_{\ell=k} \partial_y \partial_{W_k} f_{W_k}(y_{k-1})[s_{k-1}^{(j,U_j)}, \Delta V_k]\\
&\quad + \alpha \mathbf{1}_{j=k} \mathbf{1}_{\ell=k} \partial^2_{W_k} f_{W_k}(y_{k-1})[\Delta U_k, \Delta V_k].
\end{align*}
Since \(h_0^{(j,\ell;U_j,V_\ell)}=0\) and \(s_{k-1}^{(j,U_j)}=0\) for \(j\ge k\), we have:
\begin{itemize}
\item Case A (\(j,\ell<k\)): \(h_k = J_k h_{k-1} + \alpha \partial_y^2 f[s_{k-1}^{(j)}, s_{k-1}^{(\ell)}]\).
\item Case B (\(j=k,\ell<k\)): \(h_k = \alpha \partial_y \partial_{W_k} f[s_{k-1}^{(\ell)}, \Delta U_k]\).
\item Case C (\(\ell=k,j<k\)): \(h_k = \alpha \partial_y \partial_{W_k} f[s_{k-1}^{(j)}, \Delta V_k]\).
\item Case D (\(j=\ell=k\)): \(h_k = \alpha \partial^2_{W_k} f[\Delta U_k, \Delta V_k]\).
\item Case E (\(j>k\) or \(\ell>k\)): \(h_k = 0\).
\end{itemize}

\bf} 
{Stage 2: Closed-form expansion.}
We unroll the recursion from the first nonzero layer to layer \(K\).

\emph{Case \(j<\ell\).} The first nonzero term occurs at \(k=\ell\) in Case C:
\begin{align*}
h_\ell^{(j,\ell;U_j,V_\ell)} = \alpha \partial_y \partial_{W_\ell} f_{W_\ell}(y_{\ell-1})[s_{\ell-1}^{(j,U_j)}, \Delta V_\ell].
\end{align*}
For \(k=\ell+1,\ldots,K\), Case A adds the source term
\(\alpha \partial_y^2 f_{W_k}[s_{k-1}^{(j,U_j)}, s_{k-1}^{(\ell,V_\ell)}]\).

Iterating,
\begin{align*}
h_K^{(j,\ell;U_j,V_\ell)}
&= J_K J_{K-1} \cdots J_{\ell+1} \, \alpha \partial_y \partial_{W_\ell} f_{W_\ell}(y_{\ell-1})[s_{\ell-1}^{(j,U_j)}, \Delta V_\ell]\\
&\quad + \sum_{k=\ell+1}^{K} J_K J_{K-1} \cdots J_{k+1} \, \alpha \partial_y^2 f_{W_k}(y_{k-1})[s_{k-1}^{(j,U_j)}, s_{k-1}^{(\ell,V_\ell)}].
\end{align*}

\emph{Case \(j>\ell\).} By symmetry, \(h_K^{(j,\ell;U_j,V_\ell)} = h_K^{(\ell,j;V_\ell,U_j)}\).

\emph{Case \(j=\ell>0\).} The first nonzero term occurs at \(k=j\) in Case D:
\begin{align*}
h_j^{(j,j;U_j,V_j)} = \alpha \partial^2_{W_j} f_{W_j}(y_{j-1})[\Delta U_j, \Delta V_j].
\end{align*}
Iterating,
\begin{align*}
h_K^{(j,j;U_j,V_j)}
&= J_K J_{K-1} \cdots J_{j+1} \, \alpha \partial^2_{W_j} f_{W_j}(y_{j-1})[\Delta U_j, \Delta V_j]\\
&\quad + \sum_{k=j+1}^{K} J_K J_{K-1} \cdots J_{k+1} \, \alpha \partial_y^2 f_{W_k}(y_{k-1})[s_{k-1}^{(j,U_j)}, s_{k-1}^{(j,V_j)}].
\end{align*}

\bf} 
{Stage 3: Estimates.}
By \cref{cor:deriv} and the bound on \(s_{k-1}^{(j,U_j)}\) in \cref{cor:s-general}, we have:
\begin{align*}
\left\|\alpha \partial_y^2 f_{W_k}[s_{k-1}^{(j,U_j)}, s_{k-1}^{(\ell,V_\ell)}]\right\|_H
&\le \alpha M_f \frac{C_s^2}{K^2} = \frac{C_{yy}}{K^3},\\
\left\|\alpha \partial_y \partial_{W_\ell} f_{W_\ell}[s_{\ell-1}^{(j,U_j)}, \Delta V_\ell]\right\|_H
&\le \alpha M_{Wf} \frac{C_s}{K} = \frac{C_{yW}}{K^2},\\
\left\|\alpha \partial^2_{W_j} f_{W_j}[\Delta U_j, \Delta V_j]\right\|_H
&\le \alpha M_{WW} = \frac{C_{WW}}{K}.
\end{align*}
By \cref{cor:jacprod}, \(\|J_K \cdots J_{k+1}\|_{H\to H} \le C_J\).

\emph{Case \(j\ne \ell\).} Using the expansion for \(j<\ell\) (the case \(j>\ell\) is symmetric),
\begin{align*}
\left\|h_K^{(j,\ell;U_j,V_\ell)}\right\|_H
&\le C_J \frac{C_{yW}}{K^2} + \sum_{k=\ell+1}^{K} C_J \frac{C_{yy}}{K^3}
\le \frac{C_J C_{yW}}{K^2} + K \frac{C_J C_{yy}}{K^3}
= \frac{C_J(C_{yW}+C_{yy})}{K^2} =: \frac{C_{h1}}{K^2}.
\end{align*}

\emph{Case \(j=\ell\).} For \(j>0\),
\begin{align*}
\left\|h_K^{(j,j;U_j,V_j)}\right\|_H
&\le C_J \frac{C_{WW}}{K} + \sum_{k=j+1}^{K} C_J \frac{C_{yy}}{K^3}
\le \frac{C_J C_{WW}}{K} + \frac{C_J C_{yy}}{K^2}
\le \frac{C_J(C_{WW}+C_{yy})}{K} =: \frac{C_{h2}}{K}.
\end{align*}

There are \(K(K-1)\) pairs with \(j\ne\ell\) and \(K\) pairs with \(j=\ell\):
\begin{align*}
\Bigl\| \sum_{j=1}^{K} \sum_{\ell=1}^{K} h_K^{(j,\ell;U_j,V_\ell)} \Bigr\|_H
\le K(K-1) \frac{C_{h1}}{K^2} + K \frac{C_{h2}}{K}
\le C_{h1} + C_{h2} =: C_h.
\end{align*}

label: rem:loc
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:loc}
In the proofs of \cref{thm:lipschitz} and \cref{thm:smooth}, the $W$-regularity conditions of
\cref{as2} --- namely the bounds equation~\ref{eq:bound3}--equation~\ref{eq:bound5} on $\partial_{W_k}f_{W_k}$,
$\partial_y\partial_{W_k}f_{W_k}$, and $\partial^2_{W_k}f_{W_k}$ --- are invoked only at the
iterates $y_{k-1}$, $k=1,\ldots,K$. By \cref{cor:fwd}, every iterate satisfies
$\left\|y_{k-1}\right\|_H\le C_y$. Consequently, it suffices for the theorems that these three conditions
hold only for $y$ in the ball $\{\left\|y\right\|_H\le C_y\}$, rather than for all $y\in H$. The
$y$-regularity conditions (the first two lines of \cref{as2}, plus the bound
$\left\|f_{W_k}(y_0)\right\|_H\le C_f$) are genuinely global and are unaffected.

name: Localization of the parameter-regularity conditions

label: prop:mlp
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:mlp}
Let $H=\mathbb{R}^d$ and let the residual function be the $N$-layer MLP
\begin{align*}
f_{W_k}(y) = \sigma\bigl( W^{(N)} \sigma( \cdots \sigma(W^{(1)} y + b^{(1)}) \cdots ) + b^{(N)} \bigr),
\end{align*}
where $W_k=(W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(N)},b^{(1)},\ldots,b^{(N)})$ with
$W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(N)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ and $b^{(1)},\ldots,b^{(N)}\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
and equip $P$ with the norm
\begin{align*}
\left\|W_k\right\|_P = \max\bigl\{\|W^{(1)}\|_{(p,\mathrm{mean})\rightarrow(q,\mathrm{mean})},\ldots,\|W^{(N)}\|_{(p,\mathrm{mean})\rightarrow(q,\mathrm{mean})},\left\|b^{(1)}\right\|_H,\ldots,\left\|b^{(N)}\right\|_H\bigr\}.
\end{align*}
Suppose that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\sigma$ is twice continuously differentiable, with constants chosen so that
      \[
      \max\{1,|\sigma(0)|,\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|\sigma'(t)|\}
      \le L_\sigma,
      \qquad
      d^{1/p}\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|\sigma''(t)|
      \le M_\sigma,
      \]
      where $d^{1/\infty}=1$;
\item the internal depth $N$ is fixed and does not grow with $K$;
\item for all $\ell=1,\ldots,N$, $\|W^{(\ell)}\|_{(p,\mathrm{mean})\rightarrow(q,\mathrm{mean})}\le B_W$ and $\left\|b^{(\ell)}\right\|_H\le B_b$,
      with $B_W,B_b$ independent of $K$.
\end{enumerate}
Without loss of generality, enlarge the weight bound so that $B_W\ge1$.
The admissible parameter domain is the convex set
\[
\Omega=\left\{
W_k\in P:
\|W^{(\ell)}\|_{(p,\mathrm{mean})\rightarrow(q,\mathrm{mean})}\le B_W,\ 
\left\|b^{(\ell)}\right\|_H\le B_b,\quad \ell=1,\ldots,N
\right\}.
\]
All parameter-regularity comparisons are restricted to $\Omega$.

Then $f_{W_k}$ satisfies \cref{as2} in the localized sense of \cref{rem:loc}: the $y$-regularity
conditions hold globally, while the $W$-regularity conditions hold on the ball
$\{\left\|y\right\|_H\le C_y\}$, all with constants $L_f,M_f,C_W,M_{Wf},M_{WW},C_f$ depending only on
$N,L_\sigma,M_\sigma,B_W,B_b,C_x,C_y$, and not on $K$.

label: cor:mlp-thm
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:mlp-thm}
Let the residual function of \cref{def:resnet} be the MLP of \cref{prop:mlp}, and suppose
\cref{as1} and \cref{as3} hold (bounded input $x$; bounded, smooth loss $l$). Then the loss
$\mathcal{L}$ satisfies the conclusions of \cref{thm:lipschitz} and \cref{thm:smooth}: there exist
constants $L_{\mathrm{Lip}},L=O(1)$, independent of the depth $K$, such that $\mathcal{L}$ is
$L_{\mathrm{Lip}}$-Lipschitz and $L$-smooth in the block norm.

label: rem:remaining
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:remaining}
\Cref{as1} is a data-normalization hypothesis (bounded inputs and unit perturbation directions,
the latter by homogeneity). \Cref{as3} is a hypothesis on the loss function $l$ only, not on the
network, and is satisfied by standard choices (e.g.\ logistic or quadratic losses on a bounded
domain). Thus the only network-dependent hypothesis --- \cref{as2} --- is exactly what
\cref{prop:mlp} establishes for MLP residual blocks.

name: Attention blocks satisfy the residual regularity

title: Proof
body_md:
Row normalization bounds the query and key vectors in $\ell_\infty$, so the logits are $O(d_v)$ and
the $1/d_v$ scaling makes the argument of the softmax $O(1)$. This scaling controls the magnitude of the logits. To establish regularity of the full attention branch, we also account for its dependence on the hidden states and projection parameters. Column normalization bounds the query and key vectors in the
$(q,\mathrm{mean})$ norm, giving logits of size $O(d_v^{\max\{1,2/q\}})$, which is compensated by the
$d_v^{-\max\{1,2/q\}}$ scaling. For fixed sequence length and feature dimensions, the attention branch is jointly twice continuously differentiable in its input and projection parameters. On a bounded closed input domain and a bounded closed parameter domain, its first and second derivatives are therefore uniformly bounded in the prescribed norms. In particular, this bounds the state, parameter, and mixed derivatives required by \cref{as2}. If the architecture and domain bounds are independent of the residual depth $K$, the resulting regularity constants are independent of $K$. On convex domains, the corresponding Lipschitz inequalities follow by integration along line segments.
